newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly higher.

text.p: French shares closed slightly higher on Thursday after a series of disappointing first half results and a weaker start at Wall Street eroded initial gains.
The market jumped after the news of a 3.1 percent fall in U.S. August durable goods, which could indicate a slowdown in U.S. activity, but the gains were short-lived.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 0.73 points or 0.03 percent at 2,104.14 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,108 from 2,105 on Wednesday's close.
Alcatel Alsthom closed up 2.49 percent at 411 francs.

The share mainly rose on the back of the sale of a 25 percent stake in mobile telecoms company Cofira to British Telecommunications, a deal which will help the group to realise more asset gains than it planned for the year.
"That was very positive and puts the group back in the saddle," a broker said.
The market liked chairman Serge Tchuruk's presentation of a cut in first half losses and the expectation of a return to the black for 1996.
Generale des Eaux gained 3.18 percent to 552 after British Telecommunications Plc and Mannesmann of Germany joined its Cegetel telecommunications unit.
LVMH fell 3.9 percent to 1,058 on disappointing first half results and analysts' downgrades.
